integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the run's own application directory. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, public search, or unexplained network activity was detected.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Workflow: 165 file changes, 17 build/test/browser verification actions.
Network access limited to task-required hosts: earthquake.usgs.gov, basemaps.cartocdn.com, tiles.openfreemap.org, server.arcgisonline.com.

overall.summary: The most feature-complete app in the whole matrix: three basemaps, a globe projection, boolean filter chips and six test files. Its default 24-hour window undersells it on first paint.

standards.summary: 6,855 lines across 41 files with six test files, dedicated style modules per surface, and the largest ARIA footprint of the two runs.
strengths: Six test files, the only earthquake run with automated coverage
CSS split per surface rather than one global sheet
165 file changes with no `any`, no ts-ignore and no TODOs left behind

specification.summary: Meets every essential outcome and goes well past them with projection switching, basemap switching and orthogonal boolean filters.
strengths: Flat and globe projections plus a tectonic-plates overlay toggle
Boolean chips for significant, felt-by-people, tsunami flag, tectonic-only and in-map-view
Fit-results and reset-view controls tie the filter state back to the camera

ux.summary: The control surface is excellent, but the 24-hour default paints a nearly empty world map, which is the weakest possible first impression for a global dataset.

findings.title: Default window paints a near-empty map
findings.detail: The app opens on 24H with 237 events, so most of the map is blank and the ring of fire never appears. The sibling run opens on 7D with 2,100 points and reads instantly as a global picture. Default to 7D, or keep 24H and auto-fit the camera to the results.

findings.title: Two stacked panels cover the upper-left map area
findings.detail: The basemap/projection switcher and the magnitude key both float over the canvas and together occupy a large block of Europe and the North Atlantic. Merge them into one collapsible panel.

strengths: Timeline labelled in time-ago units rather than absolute dates
Keyboard shortcut hint surfaced inside the search field
Per-event accent bar in the list mirrors the map colour scale
Live indicator with an explicit last-updated timestamp
